subtopics.title: Sequential impact, friction and impulse graphs

task.prediction: The coupled carts moved left after impact. Which incoming momentum must have the greater magnitude? Explain before calculating.
task.prompt: A 2 kg cart approaches a 3 kg cart moving in the opposite direction at 5 m/s. They latch on a smooth horizontal rail; the first cart's speed is unknown. Immediately afterwards the coupled carts enter a rough level section and stop 0.80 m to the LEFT of its entrance. The measured kinetic friction coefficient is 0.25; g = 10 m/s². Neglect external horizontal impulse during the collision; the carts remain latched. Find the first cart's initial speed and the mechanical energy lost in the impact (not during braking). Explain why the direction of motion matters.

core2.prompt: A 4 kg cart moves right at 3 m/s and a 2 kg cart moves left at 6 m/s. They stick on a smooth level track. Neglect external horizontal impulse. Which statement is correct?
options: A. They move right at 1 m/s; 9 J is lost.
B. They stop; 54 J of kinetic energy is converted into other forms.
C. They move left at 1 m/s; 54 J is lost.
D. They stop with zero energy conversion.
